grades.quote: BF16 instructions set floating-point exception flags the same way as all other floating-point instructions in RISC-V.
grades.reason: Explains that instructions set exception flags, but not how software reads or clears them.

grades.quote: When a floating-point exception occurs, if its corresponding `Enable` bit is `1` , then a floating-point exception trap will be triggered; if its corresponding `Enable` bit is `0` , then the floating-point exception trap will not be triggered, but Set the corresponding position of the Flag field in `FCSR0` to `1` .
grades.reason: Explains conditional recording in FCSR0's Flag field, but does not explain reading or clearing accumulated flags.

grades.quote: Regarding the exponent field as an unbounded rounding of the intermediate result, when the absolute value of the result obtained exceeds the maximum finite number of the target format, an overflow exception will be notified.(This exception sets both inexact exception and flag bit)
grades.reason: Gives a specific example of flag setting during overflow, but no general status-recording or clearing mechanism.
